candidates.title: STAP2 contributes to retinal endothelial dysfunction in diabetes through CXCR4-associated signaling revealed by single-cell RNA sequencing.
candidates.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of vision loss and is driven by diabetes-induced retinal endothelial dysfunction. However, diabetes-associated transcriptional heterogeneity within retinal endothelial cells (ECs) and its molecular regulators remain incompletely understood. Retinal ECs were re-analyzed from a previously published single-cell RNA sequencing dataset of db/db and db/m mouse retinas. STAP2 expression was evaluated in db/db and streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic mouse retinas, human proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) tissue, and human retinal microvascular endothelial cells (HRMECs). Gain- and loss-of-function studies assessed endothelial proliferation, migration, angiogenic activity, retinal capillary degeneration, and vascular leakage. Transcriptomic profiling was used to identify downstream mediators. Three transcriptionally defined endothelial subclusters were identified, with EC3 predominantly represented in the diabetic group and showing relatively higher expression of signal-transducing adaptor protein 2 (STAP2). STAP2 was increased in diabetic retinas and high-glucose-treated HRMECs. STAP2 knockdown suppressed HRMEC proliferation, migration, and early tube formation in vitro and reduced acellular capillary formation and Evans blue extravasation in vivo, whereas STAP2 overexpression promoted these responses. Transcriptomic analysis identified C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 4 (CXCR4) as a candidate downstream mediator, and CXCR4 silencing attenuated STAP2-induced endothelial responses. These findings identify STAP2 as a previously unrecognized regulator associated with diabetic retinal endothelial dysfunction and reveal CXCR4-associated signaling as a potential mechanism involved in STAP2-mediated endothelial responses. This study provides new insights into endothelial regulation during diabetic vascular injury.

candidates.title: Refractory Cushing's Disease Complicated by Severe Thrombocytopenia and Pituitary Apoplexy Culminating in a Fatal Outcome: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Hypercortisolemia associated with Cushing's disease is classically recognized as a hypercoagulable state. Conversely, severe thrombocytopenia and hemorrhagic complications are exceptionally rare presentations. We report a case of a 59-year-old woman who presented with headache, proximal weakness, and Cushingoid features. Examination revealed severe Cushingoid features. Laboratory findings showed metabolic alkalosis, severe hypokalemia, and mild thrombocytopenia. Biochemical evaluation confirmed adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-dependent hypercortisolism (cortisol 157 µg/dL, ACTH 212 pg/mL), and a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan revealed a 28-mm invasive pituitary macroadenoma extending into the sphenoid sinus and left cavernous sinus. The patient was admitted to the intensive care unit for electrolyte replacement and blood pressure control. Thrombocytopenia worsened progressively alongside mucocutaneous bleeding. Diagnostic workup showed preserved megakaryopoiesis, normal ADAMTS-13 activity, absent schistocytes, and elevated factor VIII and von Willebrand factor levels, pointing toward platelet consumption driven by severe endothelial stress. Given severe tissue fragility and progressive thrombocytopenia, transsphenoidal surgery was deferred, and medical therapy with cabergoline, mifepristone, and metyrapone was initiated. However, dose escalation was halted by worsening hypokalemia and refractory symptoms. The patient developed central diabetes insipidus (DI), necessitating desmopressin. On day 29, acute neurological deterioration with a left third cranial nerve palsy occurred; repeat neuroimaging confirmed acute pituitary apoplexy. Emergency transsphenoidal decompression was deferred due to profound thrombocytopenia and carotid artery encasement. Facing refractory disease, salvage bilateral laparoscopic adrenalectomy was performed on day 31. Postoperatively, the patient developed refractory shock, ischemic hepatitis, and anuric acute kidney failure. Despite multimodal medical therapy, she succumbed to multiorgan failure on day 35. This case illustrates a rare and life-threatening presentation of Cushing's disease complicated by suspected secondary consumptive thrombocytopenia and sellar apoplexy, highlighting the critical challenges of managing fulminant hypercortisolemia when emergency neurosurgical intervention carries prohibitive operative risks. This case underscores the locally invasive behavior of some pituitary tumors and the need for multidisciplinary management of severe Cushing's disease complications.

candidates.title: Health-related quality of life with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors added to standard therapy for endometrial and cervical cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
candidates.abstract: To evaluate whether adding programmed cell death protein 1 or programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-1/PD-L1) inhibitors to standard therapy affects health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in patients with endometrial or cervical cancer. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception through September 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor plus standard therapy with the identical treatment backbone, with or without placebo. Mean differences (MDs) in change from baseline were pooled using random-effects models with the Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, and certainty of evidence was evaluated with GRADE. Nine RCTs involving 5,933 patients were included, of which seven trials comprising 4,995 patients contributed to the meta-analysis. Adding PD-1/PD-L1 inhibition did not significantly affect EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status/quality of life (MD -0.07; 95% CI -1.50 to 1.35; I²=0%; 7 studies; 4,995 patients). Results were also non-significant for physical, role, emotional, cognitive, and social functioning; lymphedema; menopausal symptoms; peripheral neuropathy; sexual worry; symptom experience; and EQ-5D health status. Certainty of evidence was moderate for global health status/quality of life and low for the remaining outcomes. Adding PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors to standard therapy did not detectably change global HRQoL, and the pooled confidence interval excluded clinically important deterioration. No functional or symptom domain differed significantly, although small effects cannot be excluded for domains informed by few trials.
candidates.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation

candidates.title: Septo-optic dysplasia and congenital panhypopituitarism associated with complicated gastroschisis.
candidates.abstract: Gastroschisis is a rare defect of the abdominal wall, rarely associated with other malformations. Septo-optic dysplasia (SOD) is a midline abnormality characterized by hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction and cerebral parenchymal abnormalities, both of unknown causes. I present the case of a preterm newborn with a weight appropriate for her gestational age and a prenatal diagnosis of gastroschisis. Surgical repair was performed 8 hours after birth. Subsequently, she developed fluid and electrolyte imbalances and polyuria; central diabetes insipidus was diagnosed based on a positive desmopressin test. A brain MRI was performed, showing findings consistent with SOD, and hormonal studies confirmed congenital panhypopituitarism. Hormone replacement therapy was initiated, and the patient's clinical course has been favorable. SOD and congenital panhypopituitarism are difficult to diagnose due to their variable and nonspecific presentation. Hypoglycemia is the predominant finding in newborns. Early detection allows for treatment and prevents irreversible complications. La gastrosquisis es un defecto infrecuente de la pared abdominal, rara vez asociado a otras malformaciones. La displasia septo-óptica (DSO) es una alteración de la línea media con disfunción hipotálamo-hipofisaria y anomalías del parénquima cerebral, ambas de causa desconocida. Se presenta el caso de una recién nacida pretérmino, con peso adecuado para la edad gestacional y diagnóstico prenatal de gastrosquisis. El cierre quirúrgico se realizó a las 8 horas de vida. Posteriormente, presentó alteraciones hidroelectrolíticas y poliuria; se diagnosticó diabetes insípida central mediante prueba de desmopresina positiva. Se efectuó resonancia magnética cerebral compatible con DSO y estudios hormonales que confirmaron panhipopituitarismo congénito. Se inició tratamiento de reemplazo hormonal con buena evolución clínica. La DSO y el panhipopituitarismo congénito son de diagnóstico complejo por su presentación variable e inespecífica. En neonatos predominan las hipoglucemias. El reconocimiento temprano permite su tratamiento y previene secuelas irreversibles.

candidates.title: Predicting long-term tumor response to Gamma Knife radiosurgery in vestibular schwannoma: an integrated model of auto-segmentation, MRI radiomics, and dosimetric parameters.
candidates.abstract: Vestibular schwannoma (VS) is a common benign intracranial tumor for which Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) is an important treatment option. However, post-treatment changes in tumor volume vary considerably and can complicate follow-up and response assessment. This study developed a framework that uses deep learning-based segmentation and MRI radiomics to predict long-term treatment response to GKRS for VS. We developed an nnU-Net model to automate VS segmentation on contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI. Patients with long-term follow-up after GKRS were classified into four response patterns: direct regression, delayed regression, stable disease, and growth. A two-stage machine-learning framework was then constructed. Stage 1 distinguishes regression from non-regression, while Stage 2 differentiates direct from delayed regression. Pretreatment MRI radiomics features were combined with clinical and dose-related variables and used to train multiple machine-learning models. The models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation, and SHAP analysis was used to interpret the results. The nnU-Net model achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 91.16 ± 0.47% on the external test dataset. Among the 155 patients, 53 showed direct regression, 83 delayed regression, 9 stable disease, and 10 tumor growths. In Stage 1, the Balanced Random Forest algorithm achieved accuracy of 74.19 ± 7.21%, an AUROC of 72.43 ± 10.18%, and AUPRC of 93.08 ± 4.27%. In Stage 2, the Support Vector Machine achieved accuracy of 64.05 ± 4.16%, an AUROC of 66.70 ± 6.21%, and AUPRC of 57.10 ± 7.30%. SHAP analysis identified radiomics and dose-related features as important predictors. Deep learning-based segmentation combined with pretreatment MRI radiomics, clinical variables, and dose-related parameters may provide useful information for predicting long-term response after GKRS for VS. This framework could support more individualized follow-up planning and help clinicians distinguish delayed regression from treatment failure.

candidates.title: Multidisciplinary Approach to Functioning Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors.
candidates.abstract: Functioning pituitary neuroendocrine tumors require individualized multidisciplinary management because of both tumor mass effects and hormone hypersecretion. Evaluation includes biochemical assessment of hormone excess, pituitary imaging, visual and cranial nerve examination, and assessment of comorbidities. Surgical resection, most commonly via an endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal approach, is the primary treatment for most functioning tumors. However, prolactinomas are generally treated with dopamine agonists, whereas surgery is typically first-line for growth hormone-, adrenocorticotropic hormone-, and thyroid-stimulating hormone-secreting tumors. Persistent or recurrent disease may require repeat surgery, medical therapy, or radiation.

candidates.title: Pituitary Apoplexy: Urgent Diagnosis and Surgical Intervention.
candidates.abstract: Pituitary apoplexy is an acute hemorrhagic and ischemic event, most often within a pituitary neuroendocrine tumor, that can cause sudden headache, vision loss, ophthalmoplegia, and adrenal insufficiency. Early recognition, prompt glucocorticoid replacement for unstable patients, urgent MRI for characterization, and rapid multidisciplinary coordination are critical. Urgent endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal decompression is indicated for severe or progressive vision loss, declining consciousness, or worsening cranial neuropathies. Conservative management with close observation is selected for patients with mild symptoms who are hemodynamically and neurologically stable. Modern endoscopic techniques enable excellent hematoma evacuation, optic apparatus decompression and restoration of vision and cranial nerve function. Endocrine deficits frequently persist, and require long‑term pituitary hormone replacement with multidisciplinary clinical follow‑up.

candidates.title: Subarachnoid Pneumocephalus Following Endoscopic Transsphenoidal Surgery.
candidates.abstract: A 26-year-old man with past medical history of prolactinoma presented two weeks status post endoscopic transsphenoid prolactinoma excision with a positional headache and cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea; he was found to have diffuse subarachnoid air. There are few reports of subarachnoid pneumocephalus in the emergency medicine literature. Pneumocephalus, particularly tension pneumocephalus, typically occurs in the setting of traumatic skull fractures. However, emergency physicians should be aware of subarachnoid pneumocephalus in the setting of endoscopic skull base surgeries.
candidates.journal: Clinical practice and cases in emergency medicine

candidates.title: The unseen risk: a systematic review of the incidence, management, and outcomes of the trigeminocardiac reflex in skull-base surgery.
candidates.abstract: This study synthesizes contemporary evidence on the trigeminocardiac reflex (TCR) during skull-base and adjacent neurosurgical procedures, with emphasis on operative corridors, triggers, hemodynamic phenotypes, management, and the limits of current outcome evidence. Following PRISMA guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase through September 15, 2024. Eligible reports described intraoperative TCR or closely related trigeminal autonomic responses during skull-base surgery or adjacent procedures and reported event features, management, or outcomes. Twenty-eight studies including 329 patients met inclusion criteria. Reported TCR events clustered in microvascular decompression for trigeminal neuralgia (n=168; 51.1%), CPA/posterior fossa or anterior skull-base tumor surgery (n=71; 21.6%), transsphenoidal pituitary procedures (n=47; 14.3%), and percutaneous trigeminal procedures (n=35; 10.6%). Immediate cessation of the provoking maneuver was the cornerstone of management, with anticholinergics, vasoactive agents, or temporary pacing required only in selected severe or recurrent cases. No TCR-attributable mortality was reported. However, evidence regarding long-term functional outcomes remains limited, inconsistently reported, and largely dependent on historical vestibular schwannoma and pituitary cohorts. A procedure-specific synthesis identifies high-risk maneuvers, preventive considerations, and escalation options for each operative corridor. TCR should be anticipated during trigeminal manipulation across skull-base surgical corridors and managed initially by immediate cessation or modification of the provoking stimulus, with pharmacologic or resuscitative escalation reserved for persistent or severe events. Although the available evidence supports a procedure-specific approach to prevention and preparedness, heterogeneous definitions, retrospective designs, and incomplete denominators preclude reliable incidence estimates or validated management recommendations.

candidates.title: Pediatric Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor With Extensive Necrosis: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: We describe an unusual presentation of a pediatric pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (PitNET). A 17-year-old previously healthy male presented to the emergency department with altered mental status, lethargy, nausea, vomiting, fever, and tachycardia. Head imaging incidentally demonstrated a large expansile sellar/suprasellar cystic and solid mass displacing the optic chiasm, invading bilaterally into the cavernous sinuses, and encasing the internal carotid arteries. He developed decreased vision of the left eye on hospital day two and underwent urgent endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal resection of the mass. Pathology demonstrated a PitNET with extensive necrosis, lactotroph differentiation, and changes suggestive of superimposed tumoral infection. His postoperative course was complicated by panhypopituitarism, chronic diabetes insipidus, and a cerebrospinal fluid leak managed with lumbar drainage. His presenting symptoms resolved completely, with no tumor recurrence at two-month follow-up. The initial clinical manifestation in this case was suggestive of adrenal crisis secondary to pituitary hypofunction and secondary adrenal insufficiency, attributed to significant tumor compression and pituitary necrosis, and surgical decompression was performed for new visual loss.

candidates.title: [A recently described new autoinflammatory disease (VEXAS syndrome)].
candidates.abstract: VEXAS syndrome is a recently described autoinflammatory disease characterized by specific blood count abnormalities and systemic inflammatory symptoms. In addition to autoinflammatory features and cytopenias, the clinical picture may include a wide variety of symptoms and organ manifestations, making an early diagnosis difficult. In this work, we present the first published VEXAS case in Hungary, and we detail the diagnostic process and the treatment of VEXAS syndrome. In cases of fever of unknown origin, the differential diagnosis must include autoinflammatory conditions in addition to other common causes and diseases. Bone marrow biopsy and genetic testing are essential when VEXAS syndrome is suspected. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(47): 1918-1924. A VEXAS-szindróma egy közelmúltban leírt autoinflammatiós kórkép, amelyet szisztémás gyulladásos tünetegyüttes és típusos vérképeltérések jellemeznek. Autoinflammatiós jellemzőkön és cytopeniákon túl a klinikai képet rendkívül szerteágazó tünetek, szervi manifesztációk alkotják, ezzel nehezítve a korai diagnózist. Jelen munkánkban tudomásunk szerint az első hazai VEXAS-szindrómás esetet mutatjuk be, ismertetve a betegség kivizsgálását és kezelését. Ismeretlen eredetű láz differenciáldiagnosztikája során egyéb, gyakori kórképeken túl autoinflammatiós szindrómáknak is fel kell merülniük. VEXAS-szindróma gyanúja esetén nélkülözhetetlen a csontvelő-biopszia és a genetikai vizsgálat. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(47): 1918–1924.

candidates.title: Papillary craniopharyngioma mistaken for recurrent Rathke's cleft cyst: a case report of a seven-year diagnostic pitfall involving BRAF V600E testing.
candidates.abstract: Rathke's cleft cysts (RCC) and craniopharyngiomas are clinically, radiologically and histopathologically similar lesions that are difficult to distinguish and require different surgical treatments. Many authors support the hypothesis that these represent two spectra of the same pathology. We present the case of a 53-year-old man who, because of general malaise, was examined by an endocrinologist and found to have partial hypopituitarism and indirect hyperprolactinemia. Consequently, he underwent a head MRI, which revealed an intra-suprasellar cystic lesion. Surgical fenestration of the cyst was performed, and tissue samples were collected for histopathological examination, which confirmed a diagnosis of RCC. Over the years, follow-up imaging revealed a recurrent, enlarging cyst; therefore, the patient underwent reoperation 7.5 years later. This time, histology revealed a papillary craniopharyngioma (PC). Re-examination of the specimen from the first surgery also confirmed presence of PC on the same specimen section as RCC, with the initial false-negative result attributed to suboptimal staining. Apparent progression from RCC to craniopharyngioma should prompt re-examination of the original pathology before it is interpreted as true transformation. In our patient, conservative fenestration was followed by recovery of corticotroph function that lasted seven years, whereas subsequent radical surgery resulted in new corticotroph and thyrotroph deficiency without complete resection, highlighting the need for caution with early aggressive surgery in cystic sellar lesions of uncertain histology.

candidates.title: Pituicytoma Presenting With Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism in a Highly Vascular Sellar and Suprasellar Mass: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Pituicytoma is a rare low-grade tumor arising from the pituicyte lineage of the posterior pituitary and infundibular region. Because its clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features overlap with those of more common sellar tumors and because it is often highly vascular, preoperative diagnosis and surgical management can be challenging. We presented a 45-year-old man who presented with four years of fatigue, reduced libido, erectile dysfunction, and intermittent frontal headache. Early-morning biochemical testing showed low total testosterone (8.9 nmol/L), with inappropriately normal luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), consistent with secondary hypogonadism. Pituitary magnetic resonance imaging showed a 25 × 28 × 27 mm sellar and suprasellar mass with cavernous sinus extension and superior displacement of the optic chiasm; radiologically, the lesion was initially interpreted as a pituitary macroadenoma. Because of concern regarding vascularity, computed tomography (CT) cerebral angiography was performed and demonstrated a hypertrophied right meningo-hypophyseal trunk supplying the tumor. Due to the anticipated risk of major intraoperative hemorrhage, partial surgical debulking was performed. Histopathology and immunohistochemistry supported the diagnosis of pituicytoma. Testosterone replacement increased serum testosterone. Six weeks after surgery, the patient developed secondary adrenal insufficiency and was commenced on hydrocortisone replacement. Radiotherapy was planned for the substantial residual tumor. This case highlights the importance of considering pituicytoma in the differential diagnosis of an enhancing sellar or suprasellar mass with pituitary dysfunction, particularly when marked vascularity is suspected. Preoperative vascular assessment and multidisciplinary management are important when complete resection may carry substantial hemorrhagic risk.

candidates.title: Case Report: A novel exon 1 splicing mutation in the non-coding region of the NR5A1 gene causing 46,XY disorders of sex development.
candidates.abstract: NR5A1 plays a critical role in sex differentiation and adrenal development. As a transcription factor, it regulates multiple genes involved in reproductive and endocrine processes. Mutations in NR5A1 are commonly associated with disorders of sex development and adrenal insufficiency, and most reported variants are located in coding regions. A de novo NR5A1 c.-16 + 1G > A mutation was identified in a 2-year-old patient who was gender-ambiguous. To investigate the pathogenicity and underlying mechanism of this non-coding variant, in vitro constructs with exon 1, intron 1, and exon 2 regions, including the splice sites, were generated by a minigene assay. Reverse transcription quantitative PCR was used to compare transcript expression between wild-type and mutant-type. The c.-16 + 1G > A mutation caused aberrant alternative splicing, introducing a novel start codon within intron 1 that led to premature termination in exon 2, producing a truncated protein distinct from the canonical NR5A1 protein. RT-qPCR analysis demonstrated an approximately 75% reduction normal of NR5A1 mRNA expression. These findings indicate that this mutation alters protein structure and significantly decreases normal transcript levels. The functional evidence suggests that the NR5A1 c.-16 + 1G > A non-coding region variant results in aberrant splicing and decreased expression. This variant may lead to loss of function, impairing testicular development while sparing adrenal function. These findings assist in the classification of this non-coding region NR5A1 mutation and may inform clinical management and decision-making.

candidates.title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of older adults who underwent endoscopic endonasal surgery for symptomatic Rathke cleft cysts.
candidates.abstract: Rathke cleft cysts (RCCs) are benign cystic lesions in the sellar and suprasellar regions that are often asymptomatic but may cause symptoms due to the compression of adjacent structures. With the aging of population, the incidence of symptomatic RCCs in older adults is increasing. This study aimed to compare the clinical characteristics, surgical outcomes, and follow-up between older and younger adult patients systematically. A retrospective analysis was conducted on patients aged ≥ 18 years who underwent endoscopic endonasal surgery (EES) for RCCs at a single center from 2011 to 2023. Patients were categorized into two groups: nonelderly (18-59 years) and elderly (≥ 60 years). A total of 153 patients were analyzed, with 120 younger and 33 older adult patients. Older adults presented more frequently with dizziness and fatigue. The elderly group had a shorter operation time, whereas the other surgical outcomes were similar between the two groups. The incidences of perioperative diabetes insipidus and mortality during follow-up were significantly higher in the elderly group. The recurrence rate was also higher, but no significant difference was observed. In multivariable Fine-Gray competing risk analysis, older age (adjusted SHR: 3.99, 95% CI: 1.45-11.00, p = 0.007) and cyst location, including both suprasellar (adjusted SHR: 12.70, 95% CI: 1.39-115.00, p = 0.024) and sellar-suprasellar extension (adjusted SHR: 8.67, 95% CI: 1.09-68.70, p = 0.041; vs. sellar), were associated with recurrence, whereas preoperative hypopituitarism was not (adjusted SHR: 2.20, 95% CI: 0.76-6.36, p = 0.200). EES is safe and effective for elderly patients with symptomatic RCCs. Elderly patients often present with atypical symptoms, leading to a delayed diagnosis. RCCs seem to be more likely to recur in older patients than in younger adults; thus, more careful monitoring and longer follow-up period is needed on the older adults.

candidates.title: When Thyrotropin Meets Growth Hormone: The Clinical Challenges of a Mixed GH/TSH-Secreting PIT1-Lineage Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumour.
candidates.abstract: Background: Acromegaly is most commonly caused by a growth hormone (GH)-secreting pituitary neuroendocrine tumour (PitNET). Plurihormonal PIT1-lineage PitNETs are uncommon, and combined GH and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) secretion poses distinctive diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We report a mixed GH/TSH-secreting PIT1-lineage PitNET in which the biochemical response to preoperative lanreotide supported the clinical suspicion of a functionally relevant thyrotroph component before targeted pathological reassessment. Case Presentation: A 39-year-old woman presented with a two-year history of progressive acral enlargement, headaches, hyperhidrosis, snoring, and voice deepening. Biochemical evaluation showed IGF-1 1128 ng/mL (reference range 93.1-281), GH 61 µg/L, TSH 1.5 µIU/mL (0.35-4.94), FT4 1.66 ng/dL (0.7-1.5), and FT3 7.0 pg/mL (1.8-4.2). Pituitary MRI demonstrated a 15 × 14 × 10.5 mm macroadenoma. Lanreotide 120 mg every four weeks reduced IGF-1 to 846 ng/mL and GH to 14 µg/L while normalizing FT4 (1.04 ng/dL) and FT3 (3.9 pg/mL), reinforcing the suspicion of mixed GH/TSH secretion. Transsphenoidal surgery was performed in October 2024. The tumour was initially classified as a densely granulated somatotroph PitNET; prompted by the preoperative biochemical phenotype, additional β-TSH immunostaining demonstrated positivity in numerous tumour cells, leading to reclassification as a mature plurihormonal PIT1-lineage PitNET (Ki-67 approximately 1%). Postoperative biochemical remission was not achieved, and MRI demonstrated a 7 mm residual lesion. Lanreotide was resumed, with the sustained control of the thyrotroph component but persistent GH/IGF-1 excess. Because residual disease persisted with slight cavernous sinus extension, Gamma Knife radiosurgery was performed in July 2026. Conclusions: Mixed GH/TSH-secreting PIT1-lineage PitNETs may be overlooked when TSH is inappropriately normal rather than frankly elevated. This case illustrates the value of integrating biochemical findings, treatment response, and targeted histopathological reassessment. Persistent disease despite surgery and somatostatin receptor ligand therapy further highlights the frequent need for multimodal, long-term management.

candidates.title: Giant adrenal teratoma mimicking renal angiomyolipoma during pregnancy with coexisting fetal pulmonary sequestration: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal tumors during pregnancy are rare, but their detection is increasing due to prenatal imaging. Retroperitoneal fat-containing tumors, such as mature teratomas, can easily mimic renal angiomyolipoma (RAML), especially when the gravid uterus displaces anatomical landmarks. Excluding functional tumors (e.g., pheochromocytoma) is critical to prevent lethal hypertensive crises and guide multidisciplinary team (MDT) management. A 31-year-old primigravida (12 weeks' gestation) presented with a 9.8 × 13.3 × 10.9 cm fat-containing right retroperitoneal mass on MRI, mimicking renal angiomyolipoma or teratoma. Concurrently, fetal ultrasound at 22 + 4 weeks identified an incidental left-sided fetal pulmonary sequestration. Normal catecholamine and cortisol levels confirmed a non-functional tumor, warranting a multidisciplinary team (MDT) strategy of watchful waiting. The patient successfully delivered a live infant via elective cesarean section at 37 + 1 weeks. Postpartum, she underwent elective laparoscopic resection of the retroperitoneal tumor. Intraoperatively, the massive tumor encased the inferior vena cava (IVC) and right renal vein with dense adhesions. A laceration occurred on the posterior wall of the IVC during dissection, which was successfully repaired using vascular sutures without significant blood loss (200 mL). Postoperative pathology confirmed a mature adrenal teratoma. Both mother and neonate showed excellent outcomes during follow-up. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of differentiating giant fat-containing retroperitoneal tumors during pregnancy. For non-functional retroperitoneal tumors without signs of malignancy, delaying surgery until the postpartum period is a safe strategy. In cases involving major vascular encasement, the surgical team must be fully prepared to manage unexpected vascular injuries. A multidisciplinary approach is highly recommended to optimize outcomes for rare maternal tumors and incidental fetal anomalies.

candidates.title: Oral and maxillofacial manifestations of acromegaly and their association with disease activity: a chart review.
candidates.abstract: Acromegaly is a rare endocrine disorder characterized by excessive growth hormone (GH) secretion. Facial feature modifications are the patients' most frequently reported complaint. The aim was to review the oral and maxillofacial features of acromegalic patients in a population evaluated by an oral and maxillofacial surgeon and, as a secondary. objective, to compare these manifestations according to disease activity. A chart review was conducted in two tertiary referral hospitals, including all acromegalic patients referred to the oral and maxillofacial surgery department between July 2019 and December 2024. Demographic, clinical and radiographical assessments data were collected. A total of 64 patients were included. Macroglossia was the most frequently found feature since 51 (79.6%) patients were affected. More than half the population showed a class III malocclusion, which was linked to a prognathism. The most frequent transversal malocclusion was mandibular transversal excess, which affected 25 (39%) patients. Twelve patients (18.7%) suffered from temporomandibular joint disorders (TMD). The average number of missing teeth was 4.70. Twenty-five patients (39%) exhibited periodontal disease. A total of 30 (46.8%) patients showed an interdental diastema. Fourteen (22.2%) patients exhibited oral tori. Acromegalic patients may exhibit various oral and maxillofacial manifestations beyond the stereotypical mandibular prognathism, mandibular diastemata, and macroglossia. Mandibular expansion occurs not only in the sagittal but also in the transverse dimension, making management more challenging. Although a low prevalence of TMD was observed in this population despite the presence of several potential risk factors, the present findings do not support a protective effect of GH secretion on the periodontium or temporomandibular joints, and such an effect remains speculative. Jaw and occlusal modifications may be managed with orthodontic treatment combined with orthognathic surgery.

candidates.title: Two cases of gigantism with divergent long-term outcomes: the impact of genetics and treatment adherence.
candidates.abstract: Gigantism is a rare disorder caused by growth hormone excess before epiphyseal closure. Long-term follow-up data are limited, particularly regarding the influence of genetic background and treatment adherence on disease outcomes. We report two adolescents diagnosed with gigantism during puberty who were followed at a tertiary endocrinology center for 12 and 21 years, respectively. Diagnosis was established based on elevated insulin-like growth factor 1 levels, failure of growth hormone suppression during oral glucose tolerance testing, and pituitary magnetic resonance imaging findings. Case l,a 14-year-old female, presented with accelerated linear growth, whereas Case 2, a 14-year-old male, was diagnosed following an orthopedic complication. Both patients had pituitary macroadenomas and underwent transsphenoidal surgery followed by treatment with somatostatin analogs. Germline genetic analysis of the AIP and MEN1 genes was performed using Sanger sequencing of coding exons and flanking regions from DNA extracted from peripheral blood leukocytes. One patient achieved sustained biochemical and structural remission after surgery and long-term somatostatin analog therapy, leading to treatment discontinuation. The other patient exhibited poor treatment adherence, persistent hormonal hypersecretion, residual tumor, and progressive systemic complications. Genetic analysis identified a pathogenic germline AIP nonsense variant (c.804C>A; p.Tyr268*) in the patient with unfavorable clinical evolution, whereas no pathogenic variants were detected in the other case. These findings illustrate divergent clinical trajectories in gigantism and highlight the combined impact of genetic background and treatment adherence on long-term outcomes, supporting the importance of genetic evaluation and sustained follow-up in early-onset disease.

candidates.title: Case report: Glycemic instability despite fasting C-peptide recovery during sequential somatostatin receptor ligand therapy in acromegaly with diabetes.
candidates.abstract: Somatostatin receptor ligands (SRLs) may improve glucose metabolism by reducing growth hormone excess, but they can also suppress insulin secretion. Severe hyperglycemia is well recognized with pasireotide. Less is known about glycemic stability after recovery from severe decompensation and during later changes in SRL therapy. A 32-year-old woman with diabetes had persistent acromegaly despite transsphenoidal surgery, Gamma Knife radiosurgery, cabergoline, octreotide, and lanreotide. Pasireotide long-acting release 40 mg lowered growth hormone and insulin-like growth factor 1, but approximately 1 month later was followed by diabetic ketoacidosis and a fasting C-peptide of 0.38 ng/mL. Pasireotide was stopped, insulin-based treatment was given, and octreotide was resumed. Fasting C-peptide increased to 3.09 ng/mL within 2 months. During lanreotide re-exposure in 2025, HbA1c was 9.3% despite fasting C-peptide within the reference interval and no parallel deterioration in biochemical disease control. After lanreotide withdrawal and adjustment of diabetes therapy, intermittent hyperglycemia continued, although HbA1c decreased to 6.3% by July 2026. Return of fasting C-peptide into the reference interval after pasireotide-associated diabetic ketoacidosis did not predict sustained glycemic stability in this patient. The later deterioration during lanreotide therapy was temporally associated with treatment but does not establish causality. The overall course is more consistent with persistent metabolic vulnerability despite normalization of fasting C-peptide than with confirmed recurrent SRL-induced dysglycemia. Glucose monitoring should be intensified when an SRL is started or changed in patients with diabetes or previous ketosis.

candidates.title: Role of Endocrine Testing and Preoperative Hormonal Assessment.
candidates.abstract: This article outlines a structured approach to managing patients with pituitary masses across preoperative, perioperative, and postoperative phases. It emphasizes accurate baseline hormonal assessment, appropriate correction of deficiencies before surgery, and individualized treatment strategies based on tumor type. Early postoperative care focuses on targeted hormonal monitoring to promptly identify adrenal insufficiency and arginine vasopressin deficiency, allowing timely intervention. Long-term management involves periodic reassessment of pituitary function, adjustment of hormone therapy, and ongoing surveillance for recurrence or complications, especially in hormonally active tumors.

candidates.title: A dynamic network analysis of anxiety-related distress within a quality-of-life framework among adults undergoing chemotherapy.
candidates.abstract: To understand anxiety-related distress within the quality-of-life context, this study examined how anxiety-related distress is positioned in the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire (EORTC QLQ) framework, and assessed its strongest associations with other quality-of-life factors over time. This secondary analysis of randomized controlled trial data included 390 adults aged ≥ 50 years (63.1% female) who were assessed across six time points: before chemotherapy (baseline, T1) and during chemotherapy (T2-T6). Longitudinal network analysis was used to evaluate the position and associations of anxiety-related distress, represented by worry and tension, within the EORTC-QLQ framework. A baseline network using all 30 EORTC-QLQ items first identified the position of anxiety-related distress. A reduced longitudinal network using key nodes was then estimated to examine contemporaneous, between-person, and temporal associations over time. The baseline network revealed that worry played a central bridging role within the quality-of-life framework. In the reduced longitudinal network, the strongest evidence emerged in the contemporaneous and between-person networks. At the same assessment occasion, worry and tension were positively associated with depressed mood, trouble sleeping, irritability, difficulty concentrating, and financial difficulties. At between-person level, higher average worry was associated with higher average tension, depressed mood, and financial difficulties; while higher average tension was associated with higher average irritability, worry, and difficulty concentrating. In the temporal network, financial difficulties significantly predicted higher subsequent worry but lower subsequent tension. Anxiety-related distress was centrally embedded within the EORTC QLQ framework, with worry serving as a key connector linking emotional, cognitive, sleep-related, and financial concerns. Potential leverage points for supportive care during chemotherapy were identified. ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT05838638; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05838638?term=NCT05838638&rank=1 . Anxiety-related distress is common during chemotherapy, but how it relates to other aspects of quality of life remains unclear. This study examined whether worry and tension were connected with other aspects of quality of life, including symptoms, daily functioning, mood, sleep, concentration, and financial difficulties during cancer treatment. Adults with cancer answered questionnaires once before chemotherapy and five times during treatment. We examined whether worry and tension occurred before, after, or at the same time as other quality-of-life concerns. Before chemotherapy, worry played a central role at baseline, connected with many quality-of-life concerns. During treatment, worry and tension often occurred alongside depressed mood, sleep problems, irritability, difficulty concentrating, and financial difficulties. Patients who generally reported more worry and tension also tended to experience more of these concerns across treatment. Financial difficulties at one assessment were followed by greater worry but less tension at the next assessment. These findings suggest that supportive care during chemotherapy should address worry and tension together with patients’ emotional, cognitive, sleep, functional, and financial concerns.
candidates.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation

candidates.title: Pituitary Stalk Interruption Syndrome Presenting as Primary Amenorrhea: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Demonstration of the Characteristic Diagnostic Triad.
candidates.abstract: Pituitary stalk interruption syndrome (PSIS) is a rare congenital pituitary malformation characterized by the triad of anterior pituitary hypoplasia, an absent or interrupted pituitary stalk, and an ectopic posterior pituitary. We report the case of a 21-year-old woman who presented with primary amenorrhea and poorly developed secondary sexual characteristics. Hormonal evaluation revealed central hypothyroidism, markedly reduced morning serum cortisol, and suppressed gonadotropin levels, indicating hypopituitarism with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Pelvic ultrasonography demonstrated a markedly hypoplastic uterus and bilaterally small ovaries. Magnetic resonance imaging of the sellar region revealed a hypoplastic anterior pituitary gland, nonvisualization of the pituitary stalk, and an ectopic posterior pituitary bright spot at the median eminence beneath the optic chiasm. These characteristic imaging findings established the diagnosis of PSIS. This case highlights the importance of considering PSIS in women presenting with primary amenorrhea and delayed pubertal development. Recognition of the characteristic magnetic resonance imaging triad facilitates timely endocrine evaluation, hormone replacement therapy, and long-term follow-up. RésuméLe syndrome d’interruption de la tige pituitaire (SITP) est une malformation congénitale rare de l’hypophyse, caractérisée par une triade associant une hypoplasie de l’antéhypophyse, une absence ou une interruption de la tige pituitaire et une neurohypophyse ectopique. Nous rapportons le cas d’une femme de 21 ans consultant pour une aménorrhée primaire et un développement insuffisant des caractères sexuels secondaires. Le bilan hormonal a révélé une hypothyroïdie centrale, une diminution marquée du cortisol sérique matinal et une suppression des taux de gonadotrophines, en faveur d’un hypopituitarisme associé à un hypogonadisme hypogonadotrope. L’échographie pelvienne a montré un utérus très hypoplasique et des ovaires bilatéralement de petite taille. L’imagerie par résonance magnétique (IRM) de la région sellaire a mis en évidence une hypoplasie de l’antéhypophyse, une absence de visualisation de la tige pituitaire et un hypersignal spontané T1 ectopique de la neurohypophyse au niveau de l’éminence médiane, sous le chiasma optique. Ces signes radiologiques caractéristiques ont permis d’établir le diagnostic de SITP. Ce cas souligne l’importance d’évoquer le SITP chez les femmes présentant une aménorrhée primaire et un retard du développement pubertaire. La reconnaissance de la triade caractéristique à l’IRM permet une évaluation endocrinienne précoce, l’instauration d’un traitement hormonal substitutif et un suivi à long terme.

candidates.title: Bilateral adrenal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma masquerading as bilateral adrenal metastases: a rare presentation diagnosed by endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle biopsy.
candidates.abstract: Bilateral adrenal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is an exceedingly rare entity. Presentation as bilateral adrenal masses without an identifiable extra-adrenal primary poses a formidable diagnostic challenge, frequently mimicking adrenal metastases or primary adrenal malignancy. A 70-year-old normotensive, non-diabetic male presented with a one-month history of weight loss, generalized dull abdominal pain, and anorexia. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) revealed bilateral adrenal masses (right 56 × 28 × 55 mm; left 61 × 30 × 54 mm) with imaging characteristics indistinguishable from metastatic disease. Extensive workup-including CT of the neck and chest, colonoscopy, and biochemical adrenal profiling-failed to identify a primary extra-adrenal malignancy or hormonal excess. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle biopsy (EUS-FNB) using a 22-gauge needle provided tissue confirming diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) with CD20 and PAX-5 positivity. The patient was referred to oncology and commenced on rituximab-based chemotherapy. This case underscores the indispensable role of EUS-guided tissue sampling in the evaluation of bilateral adrenal masses when non-invasive workup is inconclusive. Early tissue diagnosis of adrenal DLBCL is critical, as it is a potentially curable disease amenable to immunochemotherapy rather than surgery.

candidates.title: Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors in the Pediatric Population.
candidates.abstract: Pediatric pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PPitNETs) are rare but present significant clinical challenges in children. Their diverse presentations necessitate comprehensive endocrinologic and radiographic evaluation. They are most commonly prolactin-secreting or adrenocorticotropic hormone-secreting. A genetic mutation can be present, particularly in young patients with aggressive disease. Management is multidisciplinary. Medical therapy is first-line treatment of prolactinomas, and surgery is first-line treatment of most other PPitNETs, with reasonable remission rates when performed in experienced centers. Long-term outcomes are favorable, although hypopituitarism and lifelong hormone replacement remain important concerns. Ongoing surveillance is essential to ensure detect recurrence, and monitor treatment-related complications.

candidates.title: Basophil Activation Testing: From Diagnostic Adjunct to Precision Allergy Management.
candidates.abstract: Basophils are rare circulating granulocytes that trigger immediate hypersensitivity reactions through IgE-mediated degranulation and also contribute to innate immunity. The basophil activation test (BAT) is a flow cytometry-based functional assay that quantifies basophil reactivity and sensitivity following allergen stimulation, offering a safe, blood-based alternative to in vivo provocation testing. This review summarizes the immunological basis of the BAT, its technical requirements, and its expanding clinical applications across food, respiratory, drug, and hymenoptera venom allergies, autoimmune chronic spontaneous urticaria, and vaccine hypersensitivity. Beyond diagnosis, the BAT increasingly supports monitoring of allergen immunotherapy and biologic treatments, prediction of reaction severity and treatment response, and personalized management decisions. Its performance varies by allergen and clinical context, and wider adoption is constrained by the absence of standardized protocols, validated cut-offs, and reference materials, as well as by basophil non-releasers and dependence on fresh viable blood. Passive BAT and mast cell activation test formats extend testing to patients in whom the conventional BAT is uninterpretable. Automated, data-driven analysis and machine learning-assisted, label-free platforms offer promising routes toward more objective, scalable interpretation. With continued standardization, harmonization, and prospective validation, the BAT is positioned not only as a diagnostic adjunct but as a platform for precision-based allergy management.

candidates.title: Identification and monitoring of immune-related adverse reactions of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors based on symptom network analysis.
candidates.abstract: PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors have become first-line cancer therapies by disrupting immune checkpoint downregulation, thereby potentiating antitumor immunity. However, this enhanced immune activation may also target normal tissues, triggering multisystemic immune-related adverse events (irAE) that complicate clinical management. Conventional pharmacovigilance analyses typically assess individual adverse events in isolation, limiting the ability to capture inter-symptom relationships. Symptom network analysis, an emerging computational approach, constructs co-occurrence networks to identify core symptoms, key associations, and bridge nodes across organ systems, thus enabling a systematic understanding of complex suspected irAE profiles. Adverse event records for six PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors were extracted from two spontaneous reporting databases: FAERS (Q1 2005-Q3 2024) and JADER (Q1 2004-Q1 2025). Potential signals were screened using reporting odds ratio(ROR), proportional reporting ratio(PRR), and multivariate gamma-Poisson shrinkage (MGPS) methods. Symptom co-occurrence networks were subsequently constructed using EBIC-GLASSO based on Tetrachoric correlation matrices, which are specifically designed for binary adverse event data and correct for attenuation due to dichotomization. Four centrality metrics-Strength, Closeness, Betweenness, and Expected Influence-were calculated via the qgraph package. The bootnet package performed 1,000 bootstrap iterations to evaluate 95% confidence intervals for edge weights and centrality stability coefficients. In FAERS, nivolumab (48,330) and pembrolizumab (37,224) generated the highest report volumes. PD-1 inhibitor networks consistently centered on a systemic-gastrointestinal symptom cluster comprising decreased appetite, fatigue, diarrhea, and nausea, whereas PD-L1 inhibitor networks additionally featured prominent hematologic abnormalities. In JADER, interstitial lung disease and adrenal insufficiency emerged as central nodes, reflecting cross-database differences in reporting patterns and physician-initiated reporting practices. Strength and Expected Influence centrality metrics showed good to excellent stability (CS ≥ 0.672 in most networks), supporting the robustness of the core symptom clusters. Symptom network analysis effectively delineates core suspected irAE symptoms and inter-system associations for PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors. FAERS-derived networks emphasize systemic-gastrointestinal syndromes, while JADER reveals pulmonary-endocrine predominance in Japanese populations. These findings demonstrate the utility of symptom network analysis as a complementary approach to traditional pharmacovigilance for characterizing complex suspected irAE patterns across different data sources and populations.

candidates.title: When hypertensive crisis mimics septic shock: A case report of pheochromocytoma-induced severe lactic acidosis following GLP-1 receptor agonist administration.
candidates.abstract: Pheochromocytoma is a rare catecholamine-secreting tumor that may present atypically with severe lactic acidosis and systemic inflammatory features, closely mimicking sepsis and delaying diagnosis. A possible interaction with glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists has been suggested but remains poorly understood. A 48-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with acute nausea, vomiting, chills, severe abdominal pain, and hypertensive crisis within hours of self-administering tirzepatide, a dual GLP-1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor agonist. She was febrile, tachycardic, and markedly hypertensive, with severe lactic acidosis and systemic inflammatory markers suggestive of sepsis. Initial evaluation favored sepsis; however, negative cultures, sustained severe hypertension, hyperlactatemia disproportionate to perfusion status, and elevated urinary normetanephrines redirected the evaluation toward an endocrine cause. The clinical and biochemical picture supported a diagnosis of probable pheochromocytoma. Imaging revealed a fat-containing left adrenal mass initially suggestive of myelolipoma, representing a diagnostic pitfall. The patient was managed with intravenous fluids, a continuous nicardipine infusion, and oral alpha-blockade with doxazosin. Empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics were started and later discontinued as infection became unlikely. Beta-blockade was withheld until adequate alpha-blockade was achieved. Supportive care and electrolyte correction were provided. Blood pressure and lactate improved over 48 hours with clinical stabilization. The patient was discharged on oral alpha-blockade with plans for outpatient functional imaging (64Cu-DOTATATE positron emission tomography) and definitive surgical evaluation. Pheochromocytoma should be considered in patients presenting with unexplained lactic acidosis and hypertensive crisis, even when sepsis appears likely. Catecholamine-driven type B lactic acidosis can closely mimic infectious shock. Fat-containing adrenal lesions do not exclude pheochromocytoma, and biopsy should be avoided. The temporal association with GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure is hypothesis-generating and warrants further investigation as use of these agents continues to expand.

candidates.title: Diagnostic and Translational Challenges in Canine Endocrine and Neuroendocrine Neoplasms: A Comparative Pathology Perspective.
candidates.abstract: The recognition and detection of endocrine and neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) in dogs and humans is challenging. This is, in part, because some are non-functional, and where hormone hypersecretion occurs, it can lead to a great variety of clinical syndromes. Additionally, metastatic patterns vary according to the primary anatomical site, and the typically slow growth of many endocrine tumours/NENs may lead to underestimation of biological aggressiveness and misclassification as benign disease. In human medicine, diagnostic evaluation relies on a comprehensive, anatomical site-specific histopathologic framework, incorporating immunohistochemistry as formalised in the 2025 World Health Organisation classification of endocrine tumours/NENs. In contrast, veterinary diagnostic frameworks for canine endocrine tumours/NENs remain comparatively underdeveloped, with limited standardisation of terminology, grading systems, and validated cut-off values. This review aims to raise awareness of key diagnostic challenges associated with the most clinically prevalent canine endocrine tumours/NENs: insulinoma, phaeochromocytoma and cortisol-producing adrenocortical tumours. Emphasis is placed on histopathological characterisation using immunohistochemistry, drawing parallels with established human diagnostic algorithms where appropriate. By synthesising current knowledge from human and canine pathology, this review highlights critical gaps in veterinary diagnostic practice and identifies opportunities for harmonisation of classification strategies. The development of standardised diagnostic guidelines has the potential not only to improve clinical management of affected dogs but also to strengthen the translational value of spontaneous canine endocrine tumours/NENs within the field of comparative oncology and One Medicine.

candidates.title: Exploring the potential of machine learning for mapping FACT‑L to EQ‑5D‑5 L in early-stage lung cancer.
candidates.abstract: To compare conventional and machine-learning approaches for mapping Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Lung (FACT-L) scores to EuroQol five-dimension five-level questionnaire (EQ-5D-5 L) utilities in patients with early-stage lung cancer. Data from 326 hospitalized patients with confirmed stage I-II lung cancer were used to compare ordinary least squares (OLS), Ridge regression, beta regression, ordered-probit response mapping, random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), support vector regression (SVR), and neural networks using nested five-fold cross-validation. FACT-L and EQ-5D-5 L questionnaires were completed on postoperative day 2 or 3. Performance was assessed using mean squared error (MSE), root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and R[Formula: see text], with residual, calibration, subgroup, and feature-importance analyses. With the original 36 item predictors, ridge regression had the lowest MSE (0.037). Paired intervals supported an MSE improvement over OLS only for item-level ridge, not for any machine-learning model under any input setting. RF had higher MSE than OLS with domain and total-score inputs. Excluding L5 and GS7 changed point rankings but not this interval-based conclusion. Greater model complexity did not yield a consistent MSE benefit in this early-stage postoperative cohort. Item nonresponse and error at utility extremes limit broader application, and external validation remains necessary.
candidates.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation

candidates.title: Acute diencephalic syndrome after transventricular resection of giant pituitary adenomas with third ventricular extension: clinical course and association with extent of resection.
candidates.abstract: To describe acute diencephalic syndrome (ADS) after superior transventricular surgery for giant pituitary adenomas with true third-ventricular extension, and to explore the association of ADS with extent of resection in a selected cohort. We retrospectively analyzed 40 adults operated on in 2015-2025 (23 total, 17 subtotal resections; 22 anterior transcallosal and 18 transcortical transventricular approaches). Postoperative AVP-D was distinguished from multidomain ADS, graded retrospectively according to the previously published four-stage framework. Final-stage agreement was reassessed independently in all 40 patients. Postoperative AVP-D occurred in all 40 patients; four had isolated AVP-D without ADS. ADS occurred in 36/40 (90.0%): 23/23 after total and 13/17 after subtotal resection (risk difference 23.5 percentage points; 95% Newcombe CI 3.5-47.3; two-sided Fisher exact p = 0.026). Stage III-IV ADS occurred in 9/23 versus 3/17 (p = 0.179). Independent final-stage agreement was 36/40 (90.0%; linear-weighted κ = 0.926). Five patients required mechanical ventilation, and two died. ADS was frequent in this anatomically selected transventricular cohort, but the operational definition is not specific for hypothalamic injury and the observational comparison is vulnerable to confounding by indication. The observed lower ADS frequency after subtotal resection is hypothesis-generating. Prospective multicenter validation is necessary.

candidates.title: From aquaresis to antidiuresis: urine output-guided management of extreme hypernatremia (> 180 mmol/L) in central diabetes insipidus with reduced intracranial compliance: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Acute decompensation in central diabetes insipidus (CDI) is frequently misinterpreted as a disorder of serum sodium rather than real-time water balance. Reliance on sodium alone may delay recognition of ongoing aquaresis and result in inappropriate or unsafe correction strategies. In patients with intracranial pathology, reduced cerebral compliance further amplifies vulnerability to osmotic shifts, rendering both hypernatremia and its correction potentially injurious. We present a case of extreme hypernatremia developing within 24 h following desmopressin omission, highlighting urine output as the primary real-time marker of disease activity and redefining management priorities in acute CDI. A 15-year-old boy with pineal germinoma complicated by obstructive hydrocephalus and established CDI on desmopressin developed acute agitation and reduced consciousness following omission of a scheduled dose during chemotherapy. Within 24 h, serum sodium rose from 141 mmol/L to 189 mmol/L, with serum osmolality of 385 mOsm/kg. Urine osmolality remained inappropriately low (105 mOsm/kg), confirming ongoing aquaresis. Management prioritized restoration of AVP activity using intravenous desmopressin alongside hypotonic fluid replacement titrated to urine output rather than serum sodium. Following administration, urine osmolality increased to 647 mOsm/kg with abrupt reduction in urine output, representing transient desmopressin-induced antidiuresis before recurrence of dilute polyuria as pharmacological effect waned. Sodium correction was deliberately limited to < 10 mmol/L/day in view of ventricular dilatation and reduced intracranial reserve. The patient demonstrated progressive neurological recovery with stabilization of serum sodium. Subsequent evaluation revealed previously unrecognized panhypopituitarism, including central adrenal insufficiency and central hypothyroidism, necessitating sequential hormone replacement. This case demonstrates that acute CDI decompensation is fundamentally a disorder of dynamic water flux rather than isolated dysnatremia. Urine output provides the most immediate indicator of AVP activity, whereas serum sodium represents a delayed cumulative consequence. Intravenous desmopressin induces rapid shifts from uncontrolled aquaresis to transient antidiuresis, creating a narrow therapeutic window requiring careful titration. In the presence of reduced intracranial compliance, sodium correction strategies must be individualized beyond conventional time-based classifications. Structural CDI should also prompt systematic evaluation of anterior pituitary function, as global axis failure may remain clinically silent until physiological stress unmasks it. Management strategies that prioritize serum sodium over urine output risk both delayed intervention and iatrogenic overcorrection.

candidates.title: [Acute coronary syndromes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation].
candidates.abstract: Nearly half of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation have concomitant significant coronary artery disease. In patients with severe aortic stenosis and coexisting obstructive coronary artery disease, several issues remain controversial, including the optimal diagnostic evaluation, the choice of treatment strategy (surgical, percutaneous, or conservative), the indication for and extent of coronary revascularization, and, if percutaneous coronary intervention is performed, its optimal timing. After transcatheter aortic valve implantation, selective coronary cannulation may be challenging in a subset of patients, an issue of increasing clinical relevance as accumulating evidence in recent years has progressively expanded transcatheter aortic valve implantation indications to patients with longer anticipated survival. Although the likelihood of requiring invasive coronary angiography or percutaneous coronary intervention after transcatheter aortic valve implantation is expected to increase in these patients, coronary events occurring during the post-transcatheter aortic valve implantation period - particularly life-threatening acute coronary syndromes - remain insufficiently characterized with respect to their incidence, clinical characteristics, predictors, and outcomes. In addition to conventional atherothrombotic mechanisms, the transcatheter heart valve itself may contribute to the development of acute coronary syndromes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Furthermore, the presence of a transcatheter heart valve may complicate invasive management because of technical challenges related to coronary access. This may be of particular importance in patients presenting with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction after transcatheter aortic valve implantation, in whom rapid and reliable coronary access and time-critical reperfusion are essential. The Gottsegen National Cardiovascular Center is one of the leading high-volume centers nationwide for the treatment of patients with severe aortic stenosis. Since the initiation of the institutional transcatheter aortic valve implantation program in 2008, more than 3000 procedures have been performed. Analysis of this large-scale registry may contribute to a better understanding of the currently unknown incidence, clinical characteristics and outcomes of acute coronary syndromes among patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation in Hungary. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(47): 1887-1899. A transzkatéteres aortabillentyű-implantációban részesülő betegek közel fele rendelkezik szignifikáns koszorúér-betegséggel. A súlyos aortabillentyű-szűkületben és obstruktív koszorúér-betegségben is szenvedő páciensekben a koszorúér-betegség megfelelő diagnózisa, a kezelés módja (sebészi, percutan vagy konzervatív), a coronariarevascularisatio indikációja és mértéke, valamint ha percutan coronariaintervenció mellett születik javaslat, akkor annak időzítése jelenleg szakmai vita tárgya. A transzkatéteres aortabillentyű-implantáció után a koszorúerek katéteres kanülálhatósága a betegek egy részében nehezített lehet, ami egyre nagyobb jelentőséggel bír, mivel a transzkatéteres aortabillentyű-implantáció indikációs köre – az utóbbi évek tudományos eredményeinek köszönhetően – a hosszabb életkilátással rendelkező betegekre is fokozatosan kiterjed. Habár ezekben a betegekben a transzkatéteres aortabillentyű-implantációt követő invazív coronariaangiográfia vagy percutan coronariaintervenció szükségességének valószínűsége növekszik, kevésbé ismertek transzkatéteres aortabillentyű-implantáció utáni időszakban kialakult coronariaesemények – különösen az életet veszélyeztető akut coronaria szindróma – incidenciája, klinikai jellemzői, prediktorai és kimenetelei. A transzkatéteres aortabillentyű-implantációt követően kialakult akut coronaria szindróma hátterében a klasszikus atherothromboticus mechanizmusok mellett a katéteres szívbillentyű kóroki szerepe is felmerül. Ezenfelül az invazív kezelést a transzkatéteresen behelyezett szívbillentyű jelenléte okozta technikai kihívások nehezíthetik, ami különösen fontos lehet egy transzkatéteres aortabillentyű-implantáción átesett betegnél ST-elevációval járó myocardialis infarktus ellátásában, amelynél a könnyű, biztos koszorúér-kanülálás és az időkritikus reperfúzió kulcsfontosságú. A Gottsegen György Országos Kardiovaszkuláris Intézet országosan az egyik vezető, nagy volumenű centrum a súlyos aortabillentyű-szűkületben szenvedő betegek gyógyításában. Az Intézetben 2008 óta működő program keretein belül közel 3000 transzkatéteres aortabillentyű-implantáció történt; az ebből táplálkozó regiszter adatainak feldolgozása segítheti a magyarországi – jelenleg nem ismert –, transzkatéteres aortabillentyű-implantáción átesett betegek körében az akut coronaria szindróma előfordulási gyakoriságának, klinikai jellemzőinek és kimenetelének jobb megismerését. candidates.title: Deep learning MGMT promoter methylation status prediction in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma using multiparametric MRI: Benchmark vs. real‑world performance.
candidates.abstract: Preoperative determination of O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) promoter methylation status is of major prognostic and predictive relevance in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, yet currently depends on invasive tissue sampling. This study investigates deep learning-based strategies for MGMT prediction from multiparametric MRIs, with particular emphasis on robustness and generalizability under heterogeneous, multicenter conditions. A total of 949 glioblastoma cases were analyzed, integrating public benchmark data from the Brain Tumor Segmentation Challenge (BraTS) with multi-institutional private cohorts acquired across diverse scanners and imaging protocols. Four complementary experimental settings were designed to compare reproduced literature baselines, private-only training, whole-brain end-to-end models, and segmentation-guided region-of-interest (ROI) pipelines. Tumor delineation was performed using an nnU-Net framework with expert quality control, and multiple three-dimensional convolutional neural network architectures were evaluated. Model performance was highest on the homogeneous BraTS benchmark, where a whole-brain DenseNet121 achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.80. However, marked performance deterioration was observed when models were evaluated on independent held-out multicenter test set. In contrast, segmentation-guided ROI-based approaches showed a more stable performance profile in this preliminary independent held-out multicenter test. Explicit lesion localization was associated with reduction in false-positive classifications, suggesting a potential benefit for performance stability across heterogeneous datasets, although validation in external cohorts from institutions not represented during training is required. Collectively, these results demonstrate that upstream methodological choices, especially tumor segmentation and ROI definition, remain critical determinants of performance in MRI-based radiogenomic modeling. Future studies should emphasize prospective multicenter validation, domain-shift harmonization, multimodal data integration, and uncertainty-aware deep learning to enhance robustness and interpretability.

candidates.title: Autoantibodies in Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Related Endocrinopathies.
candidates.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have been established as a standard treatment for many types of cancer; however, they present a clinical challenge due to unique side effects known as immune-related adverse events (irAEs). Endocrine irAEs include the more frequently reported thyroid and pituitary dysfunctions, as well as less frequent, but potentially severe conditions, such as ICI-related type 1 diabetes and primary adrenal insufficiency. These can lead to life-threatening complications, thus requiring careful management. Their pathogenesis is thought to be an autoimmune response. Recent reports have identified various autoantibodies in patients with endocrine irAEs, drawing attention to their clinical significance. This review describes the clinical features and presumed pathogenic mechanisms of endocrine irAEs. Furthermore, it comprehensively summarizes the autoantibodies reported for each endocrine irAE and discusses their significance based on the latest findings, focusing on their utility as predictive biomarkers for irAE onset, their diagnostic value, and their potential involvement in the pathogenesis.

candidates.title: Adrenal ganglioneuroma in an adolescent presenting as an incidentaloma: Imaging-pathology correlation and diagnostic challenges: A case report.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal ganglioneuroma (AGN) is a rare, benign, and usually nonfunctioning tumor arising from neural crest-derived sympathetic ganglion cells. Preoperative diagnosis is difficult because the clinical presentation is often nonspecific, and imaging findings overlap with those of other adrenal neoplasms. We describe an adolescent adrenal incidentaloma with detailed imaging-pathology correlation, adding to the small number of reported adolescent cases. A previously healthy 16-year-old male underwent contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) after a bicycle accident. No traumatic injury was identified, but imaging incidentally revealed a well-circumscribed right adrenal mass measuring approximately 6.1 cm × 3.6 cm × 5.0 cm. CT and magnetic resonance imaging showed progressive, persistent enhancement across the arterial, venous, and delayed phases without demonstrable washout (attenuation increased from 20 Hounsfield units unenhanced to 55 Hounsfield units in the venous phase, with further qualitative enhancement on 15-minute delayed images) and no intralesional fat, suggesting a non-adenomatous lesion and raising suspicion for a neurogenic tumor. Biochemical evaluation showed no evidence of hormonal hypersecretion. Histopathological examination after resection established the diagnosis of AGN. The patient underwent right adrenalectomy because of the size and radiologically indeterminate nature of the mass. The postoperative course was uneventful. Transient elevation of blood pressure noted during follow-up prompted biochemical reevaluation, which showed no evidence of excess catecholamine. Follow-up CT at 9 months showed no recurrence. Progressive delayed enhancement without washout and absence of signal loss on opposed-phase magnetic resonance imaging, a pattern previously described in ganglioneuroma, may suggest the diagnosis preoperatively, although definitive diagnosis requires histopathological confirmation. Complete surgical excision established the diagnosis and achieved a favorable short-term outcome; the excellent long-term prognosis of AGN is supported by the published literature, and our patient remains recurrence-free at 9 months.
